prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She go to school every day.
She goes to school every day.
She going to school every day.
She gone to school every day.
explanation: With she/he/it, add -s or -es to the verb: "goes".

prompt: I ___ English every day.
explanation: With I, use the base form: "study".

prompt: They ___ in a big house.
explanation: With they, use the base form: "live".

prompt: We ___ breakfast at 7 a.m.
explanation: With we, use "have".

prompt: She ___ a book right now.
explanation: Use "is" + verb-ing for actions happening now.

prompt: They ___ dinner at the moment.
explanation: Use "are" + verb-ing with "they".

prompt: Listen! The baby ___.
explanation: With "the baby" (singular) use "is" + verb-ing.

prompt: I ___ to music now.
explanation: With "I" use "am" + verb-ing.

prompt: I ___ from Indonesia.
explanation: With "I", use "am".

prompt: My friend ___ very tall.
explanation: With "my friend" (singular), use "is".

prompt: The students ___ in the classroom.
explanation: With plural "students", use "are".

prompt: It ___ a sunny day.
explanation: With "it", use "is".

prompt: ___ a book on the desk.
explanation: Use "there is" with a singular noun: "a book".

prompt: ___ many people in the park.
explanation: Use "there are" with a plural noun: "many people".

prompt: Is ___ any milk in the fridge?
explanation: The question form uses "Is there ..." for a singular or uncountable noun.

prompt: There ___ two chairs in the room.
explanation: Use "are" with the plural "two chairs".

prompt: He ___ swim very fast.
explanation: "Can" never changes: no -s and no "to".

prompt: ___ you open the window?
explanation: Use "Can" + subject + base verb for a question.

prompt: I ___ drive a car, but I am not very good at it.
explanation: Use "can" for ability.

prompt: We ___ go to the party tonight.
explanation: "Cannot" (written as one word) means not able to.

prompt: Yesterday I ___ to the market.
explanation: "Go" is irregular; its past form is "went".

prompt: We ___ a film last night.
explanation: Regular verbs add -ed: "watched".

prompt: She ___ her homework before dinner.
explanation: "Do" is irregular; its past form is "did".

prompt: They ___ not see the bus.
explanation: Negative past uses "did not" + base verb: "did not see".

prompt: We ___ to buy a new car next month.
explanation: Use "are going to" with "we" for a plan.

prompt: Look at those clouds! It ___ rain.
explanation: Use "is going to" for a prediction based on evidence.

prompt: She ___ to become a doctor.
explanation: With "she", use "is going to".

prompt: What ___ you going to do this weekend?
explanation: With "you", use "are".

prompt: The phone is ringing. I ___ answer it.
explanation: Use "will" for a decision made at the moment of speaking.

prompt: Don't worry. I ___ help you with your homework.
explanation: Use "will" for an offer or promise.

prompt: I think it ___ rain tomorrow.
explanation: Use "will" for a general prediction after "I think".

prompt: She ___ not come to the party.
explanation: Negative future: "will not" (won't) + base verb.

prompt: My brother is ___ than me.
explanation: Short adjectives take -er: "taller".

prompt: This phone is ___ than my old one.
explanation: Long adjectives use "more": "more expensive".

prompt: Lisbon is ___ than I expected.
explanation: For short adjectives ending in one vowel + consonant, double the consonant: "hotter".

prompt: Learning English is ___ than learning Spanish.
explanation: Adjectives ending in -y change to -ier: "easier".

prompt: Tom is ___ boy in our class.
explanation: Use "the" + -est for the top of a group: "the tallest".

prompt: This is ___ film I have ever seen.
explanation: "Good" is irregular: "the best".

prompt: Paris is ___ city I have visited.
explanation: Long adjectives use "the most": "the most beautiful".

prompt: She is ___ person in the office.
explanation: Adjectives ending in -y change to -iest: "the happiest".

prompt: I ___ never ___ sushi.
explanation: Present perfect: have + past participle "eaten".

prompt: She has worked here ___ 2020.
explanation: "Since" is used with a point in time, like 2020.

prompt: They ___ already ___ their homework.
explanation: Use "have" with "they" and the past participle "finished".

prompt: We have lived in this city ___ five years.
explanation: "For" is used with a period of time: five years.

prompt: If it ___ tomorrow, we will stay home.
explanation: After "if", use the present simple, not "will".

prompt: If you heat ice, it ___.
explanation: This is a general truth, so the present simple is correct in both clauses.

prompt: I ___ you if I have time.
explanation: Result clause: "will" + base verb.

prompt: If she ___ early, she will catch the train.
explanation: After "if", use the present simple: "leaves".

prompt: The cake ___ by my sister yesterday.
explanation: Passive past: was/were + past participle "made".

prompt: English ___ all over the world.
explanation: Passive present: is/are + past participle "spoken".

prompt: These letters ___ last week.
explanation: With plural "letters", use "were" + past participle.

prompt: The bridge ___ next year.
explanation: Future passive: will be + past participle.

prompt: The girl ___ won the race is my cousin.
explanation: Use "who" for people.

prompt: I read a book ___ was very exciting.
explanation: Use "which" or "that" for things.

prompt: The restaurant ___ we ate last night was expensive.
explanation: Use "which" or "that" for places/things.

prompt: Do you know the man ___ lives next door?
explanation: "That" or "who" can be used for people in this sentence.

prompt: I ___ live in a small village.
explanation: Past habit: "used to" + base verb.

prompt: We ___ go swimming every summer when we were kids.
explanation: Use "used to" for past habits.

prompt: There ___ a cinema in this street, but it closed.
explanation: Past state: "used to be".

prompt: She ___ not ___ coffee, but now she loves it.
explanation: Negative: "did not use to" + base verb. Here "used to" is correct.

prompt: If I ___ a bird, I would fly to you.
explanation: In second conditional, "were" is used for all persons in formal English.

prompt: If we had a car, we ___ to the beach every weekend.
explanation: Result clause: would + base verb.

prompt: If he ___ harder, he would pass the test.
explanation: If-clause uses the past simple: "studied".

prompt: What ___ you do if you won a million dollars?
explanation: Use "would" in the result clause.

prompt: If I ___ earlier, I would have seen the film.
explanation: Third conditional if-clause: had + past participle.

prompt: We would have won if we ___ harder.
explanation: Use "had" + past participle in the if-clause.

prompt: If you had told me, I ___ you.
explanation: Result: would have + past participle.

prompt: She ___ the exam if she had studied more.
explanation: Result: would have passed (past participle "passed").

prompt: When I got home, the children ___ to bed.
explanation: The going to bed happened before getting home: past perfect "had gone".

prompt: By the time she arrived, the show ___ already started.
explanation: Past perfect: had + past participle "started" (had has a past form "had").

prompt: He ___ never ___ abroad before last year.
explanation: Past perfect "had been" for experience before a past point.

prompt: We ___ the house before the storm came.
explanation: Use had + past participle for the earlier action.

prompt: "I am busy," she said. → She said that she ___ busy.
explanation: Present simple "am" backshifts to past simple "was".

prompt: "I will call you," he said. → He said he ___ call me.
explanation: "Will" backshifts to "would" in reported speech.

prompt: "Where do you live?" → She asked me where I ___.
explanation: Reported questions use statement word order: "where I lived".

prompt: "Are you coming?" → He asked me ___ I was coming.
explanation: Yes/no questions are reported with "if" or "whether".

prompt: The lights are on, so someone ___ at home.
explanation: "Must be" shows a strong logical conclusion.

prompt: The shop is closed. It ___ be open on Sundays.
explanation: "Can't be" shows a strong negative guess.

prompt: He ___ have left already; I am not sure.
explanation: "Might" shows possibility; the speaker is unsure.

prompt: She missed the bus, so she ___ have been late.
explanation: Past deduction: "must have been" (the speaker is fairly sure).
